original_target.title: The $`4\pi`$ boundary-curvature threshold for oriented minimal surfaces

full_original_statement:
Let $`\Gamma\subset\mathbb R^3`$ be a smooth, simple closed curve with total *boundary-curve* curvature
```math
\mathrm{tc}(\Gamma)=\int_\Gamma |\kappa|\,ds\leq4\pi.
```

Must every smooth, compact, oriented minimal surface spanning $`\Gamma`$ be a disk? Equivalently, if such a curve bounds an oriented minimal surface that is not a disk, must $`\mathrm{tc}(\Gamma)>4\pi`$? The orientability condition matters: curves of total curvature below $`4\pi`$ can bound minimal Möbius strips.

Brian White proves the disk conclusion for $`\mathrm{tc}(\Gamma)\leq 2\pi\sqrt{2\pi/e}`$, approximately $`1.014\cdot3\pi`$, and conjectures the sharp $`4\pi`$ threshold for oriented surfaces. Curves of curvature less than $`4\pi+\varepsilon`$ can bound oriented embedded minimal surfaces of arbitrarily high genus, so the proposed constant cannot be raised.

sources.scope_comparison: The full local target requires disk topology for every compact oriented spanning minimal surface at boundary-curve total curvature <=4pi. Actual Theorem19 gives only tc>2pi sqrt(2pi/e) for oriented nondisks and explicitly conjectures replacing that smaller threshold by 4pi. An embeddedness theorem at4pi does not force disk topology; Mobius-strip examples fail orientability, and total surface Gaussian curvature results use a different invariant. No later full matching announcement was located. The supplementary Stanford lecture-note mirror returned502, but the published original theorem and conjecture were directly readable.
